sentences.text: This Writ Petition has been filed for the issue of Writ of Mandamus directing the second respondent to re-present the LAOP petition before the Subordinate Court, Tuticorin in order to enable the petitioner to prosecute the petition, wherein, the petitioner has sought for enhancement of compensation.
2.The case of the petitioner is that his lands were acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 through Notification issued in the year 1987.
The award was passed by the second respondent on 31.05.1990.
A compensation of a sum of Rs.7,58,694/- was fixed.

The petitioner and others claimants were not satisfied with this compensation and hence, the petitioner made a reference before the first respondent under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The grievance of the petitioner is that in spite of making the reference, the petitioner has not seen any progress in this case for more than thirty years, since the LAOP that was presented before the Subordinate Court was returned for compliance with certain defects and it was never represented.
It is under these c i r c u m s t a n c e s , t h e p r e s e n t W r i t P e t i t i o n h a s b e e n f i l e d b e f o r e t h i s C o u r t .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
3.When the matter came up for hearing on 04.10.2023, this Court passed the following order:

The grievance that has been expressed by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the LAOP petition that was filed in the year 2005 before the Sub Court, Tuticorin (now Sub Court, Tiruchendur), with respect to the subject property has not been properly prosecuted by the second respondent and there has been absolutely no progress for the last 18 years.
The learned counsel for the respondent is directed to take instructions in this regard and report before this Court in order to enable this Court to pass final orders in this writ petition.
Post this case finally on 11.10.2023.
4.The matter was again taken up for hearing on 11.10.2023 and this Court passed the following order:
In spite of the earlier order passed by this Court dated 04.10.2023, no proper instructions had been given by the 2nd respondent.
Hence, the 2nd respondent shall be present before this Court during the next date of hearing.
in the meantime, the second respondent shall ascertain the status of the LAOP petition that has been filed before the Sub Court, Tuticorin.
Post on 16.10.2023 under the same caption.

5.The matter was once again posted for hearing on 16.10.2023 and this Court passed the following order:

Pursuant to the earlier order passed on 11.10.2023, Mr.Gaurav Kumar, IAS, Sub Collector, Tuticorin was present before this Court.

sentences.text: 2.The learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the respondents submitted that there was some lapse in following up with the reference and sought for sometime to set right the entire process and to report before this Court.
3.A counter affidavit has also been filed by the second respondent and a copy of the same was also served on the learned counsel for the petitioner.
4.Considering the above, post this case under the same caption on 11.12.2023.
By then, the petition has to be represented before the concerned Court and it has to be numbered and informed to this Court.
Thereafter, this Court will pass further orders in this writ petition.
The appearance of the second respondent is dispensed with.

6.When the matter was taken up for hearing today, the learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the respondents submitted that the petition has been represented in Diary No.8481/2023 before the Subordinate Court, Tuticorin.

The learned Additional Advocate General further submitted that there is a delay and if no serious objections are made by the petitioner, this Court can direct the Subordinate Court, Tuticorin, to condone the delay and to proceed further to decide the LAOP on merits.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.The

learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner and the other claimants are more interested in getting enhanced compensation and they may not have any serious objections in the delay being condoned.
The learned Counsel for the petitioner however requested to fix a time frame for the completion of LAOP proceedings.

8.Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and the subsequent developments, there shall be a direction to the learned Subordinate Judge, Tuticorin, to condone the delay in representing the papers in LAOP by the second respondent.
Thereafter, LAOP shall be decided on merits and final orders shall be passed within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

It is made clear that the delay that has been caused in this case cannot be attributed to the petitioner and the other claimants and therefore, for this period of delay, they cannot be deprived of payment of interest, if ultimately, the compensation is enhanced by the reference Court.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.This
Writ Petition is disposed of in the above terms.
No costs.
